question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act restored the Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights?
solution:
The correct answer is __**24th Amendment Act, 1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **24th Amendment Act, 1971** was enacted to restore the Parliament's authority to amend the Fundamental Rights, following the ruling in the **Kesavananda Bharati Case** (1973).
 
• It was introduced as a response to the **Supreme Court judgment in Golaknath Case (1967)**, which restricted the Parliament's ability to amend Fundamental Rights.
 
• The Amendment added a new clause (4) to **Article 13**, explicitly stating that a Constitutional amendment cannot be challenged as violating Fundamental Rights.
 
• It also amended **Article 368**, explicitly stating that the Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights.
 
• The **24th Amendment** empowered the President to give his assent to Constitutional Amendment Bills, making it mandatory.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 24th Amendment Act, 1971.***</l
